answer: Through the hollow, the economy stays open to anyone willing to pay the price of entry, and closed to free clones. The network limits how much trust any single agent can pass on, so one compromised sponsor cannot flood the economy with fakes. The garden makes the attacker's problem topological: to place a thousand clones it must grow a thousand credible paths from honest agents, and honest agents do not hand out paths for free. Through the ferrous, one real agent costs once and a thousand pretenders cost a thousand times — no shortcut survives that math.
